s: God calls Jeremiah as a young man: before I formed you in the womb I knew you. Visions of an almond branch and a boiling pot.
Israel has forsaken the fountain of living water and dug broken cisterns.
Unfaithful Israel is called to return to the Lord.
Return to God with your whole heart. Disaster is coming from the north.
Not one just person can be found in Jerusalem. The people refuse correction.
Jerusalem will be besieged. The people say peace, peace, when there is no peace.
Jeremiah's temple sermon: do not trust in the temple while doing evil. It has become a den of thieves.
The people will not repent. The harvest is past and we are not saved. Is there no balm in Gilead?
Jeremiah weeps for his people. Let him who boasts boast that he knows the Lord.
Idols are nothing; the Lord is the true and living God.
The people have broken the covenant. Jeremiah's own townsmen plot against him.
Jeremiah asks why the wicked prosper. God answers that worse is to come.
A ruined linen belt is a sign of how pride will ruin Judah.
Drought comes. Jeremiah prays for the people, but false prophets promise peace.
God will not relent. Jeremiah complains of his loneliness, and God promises to make him strong.
Jeremiah is told not to marry, as a sign of coming disaster. God will one day bring Israel back.
Judah's sin is written with an iron pen. Blessed is the one who trusts in the Lord. Keep the sabbath holy.
At the potter's house: like clay in the potter's hand, so is Israel in God's hand.
Jeremiah smashes a clay jar as a sign that Jerusalem will be broken.
Pashhur puts Jeremiah in the stocks. Jeremiah complains that God's word burns like fire in his bones.
Zedekiah asks for help, but Jerusalem will fall to Babylon.
Words of judgment against the kings of Judah.
Woe to the shepherds who scatter the flock. God will raise up a righteous Branch for David. False prophets condemned.
A vision of good and bad figs: the exiles and those who remain.
Judah will serve Babylon for seventy years, and the nations will drink the cup of God's wrath.
Jeremiah is threatened with death for prophesying against the temple, but is spared.
Jeremiah wears a yoke and tells the nations to submit to Babylon.
The false prophet Hananiah breaks Jeremiah's yoke and dies that year.
Jeremiah's letter to the exiles: build houses, seek the peace of the city, for I know the plans I have for you.
God promises to bring his people home and heal their wounds.
God will make a new covenant, writing his law on their hearts. Rachel weeps for her children.
Jeremiah buys a field during the siege as a sign that the land will be restored.
God promises restoration and a righteous Branch from David.
Zedekiah is warned. The people free their slaves, then take them back.
The Rechabites' faithfulness shames Judah's disobedience.
King Jehoiakim burns Jeremiah's scroll, and Baruch writes it again.
Jeremiah is arrested and imprisoned.
Jeremiah is thrown into a muddy cistern and rescued by Ebed-melech.
Jerusalem falls. Zedekiah is blinded and taken to Babylon. Jeremiah is freed.
Jeremiah stays in the land with the governor Gedaliah.
Gedaliah is murdered by Ishmael.
The survivors ask Jeremiah for God's guidance and are told not to go to Egypt.
The people go to Egypt anyway and take Jeremiah with them.
Jeremiah condemns the Jews in Egypt for worshipping the queen of heaven.
A message of comfort for Baruch.
Prophecy against Egypt.
Prophecy against the Philistines.
Prophecy against Moab.
Prophecies against Ammon, Edom, Damascus and other nations.
Babylon will fall and Israel will return seeking the Lord.
More on Babylon's fall. Jeremiah's scroll is sunk in the Euphrates.
The fall of Jerusalem retold. King Jehoiachin is released in Babylon.

1: God knew and chose Jeremiah before he was born. It is a strong witness to the value of every human life from the womb.
31: God promises a new covenant written on hearts. Jesus speaks of the new covenant in his blood at the Last Supper.
